= Cheryl D. Edwards =
Cheryl D. Edwards (born March 18, 1954) is an American visual artist, educator and curator who lives and works in Washington, D.C. Her work has been exhibited in the United States and internationally and is held in institutional collections including the Library of Congress and the David C. Driskell Center. She has also curated exhibitions for institutions such as the Art Museum of the Americas (AMA) and George Mason University. Her curatorial project Before the Americas received international media coverage following its cancellation and subsequent exhibition at George Mason University.
Early life
Edwards was born in Miami, Florida in 1954, the year the Supreme Court's landmark ruling in Brown v. Board of Education. She grew up in Miami during the 1960s and 1970s, a period marked by civil rights activism, increased Cuban and Caribbean immigration and desegregation efforts. Edwards has described experiencing segregation during her childhood and participating in community activities, including volunteering with her family to assist migrant farm workers with government paperwork.
Edwards has stated that these experiences informed her later interests in art, education, and civil rights, as well as her emphasis on professional stability. She received a Bachelor of Arts in political science from Boston University in 1976, completed graduate studies in African American and Black Diaspora Studies, and received a Juris Doctor from Syracuse University in 1980. In the 1980s, she worked as an administrative law judge in New York City and studied in the evenings at the Art Students League of New York, where she trained under Ernest Crichlow.
In the early 1990s, she established a private law practice. She left full-time legal practice in the late 1990s and worked in management roles for government and non-profits while developing her art practice.
Career and exhibitions
Edwards began exhibiting her work in the early 2000s, including a first solo exhibition in 2005. She has since exhibited in solo and group exhibitions internationally and has received fellowships, residencies, and grants. She was represented by the Susanne Junggeburtth Gallery in Stuttgart, Germany from 2013 to 2018. She currently holds a studio space in Washington, D.C. and has shown throughout the DC metropolitan area.
Her work is held in the collections of several institutions, including the Library of Congress, the James E. Lewis Museum of Art, the Georgetown University Art Collection (Booth Family Center for Special Collections) and the David C. Driskell Center.
Awards and residencies
Edwards has received fellowships and residencies including a residency at the Experimental Printmaking Institute at Lafayette College (2015), Artist Fellowship Awards from the DC Commission on the Arts and Humanities (2015; 2021–2024), participation in the Oral Histories Art Cart Project (2016), and the Black Writers Fellowship from Hand Papermaking, Inc. (2020). She has also participated in the Arts, Letters, and Numbers Residency (2024) and received the Gamblin Art Award Fellowship at the Monte Azul Art Center in Costa Rica (2024–2025), as well as a mentorship award from George Mason University (2025). Her work has been included in books including the cover art for The Wombs of Women: Race, Capital, Feminism (2020) by Françoise Vergès   and Montana Mouthful: The Quarantine Issue. Her contributions as an art panelist were included in podcasts including an interview with Wendy Grossman for Radio France.
Institutional roles in the arts
From 2015 to 2023, Edwards served as Senior Advisor to the executive director of the David C. Driskell Center at the University of Maryland. She has held advisory and board roles with several arts organizations in the Washington, D.C., area, including the McLean Project for the Arts, the Washington Sculptors Group, the Washington Print Club, The Studio Visit (TSV), and the George Mason University Art Board. Edwards has taught courses at the Kreeger Museum and has participated in public programs and panel discussions at arts institutions in the Washington, D.C. area.
Curatorial work or projects
As an educator, artist, and advisor, Edwards' practice has expanded to include curatorial work for institutions including the Art Museum of the Americas, Gillespie Gallery, the John A. Cade Center for Fine Arts Gallery, the Joan Hisaoka Healing Arts Gallery, and the University of Maryland Global Campus (UMGC) Arts Program Gallery.
The exhibition Before the Americas was commissioned by the Art Museum of the Americas after directors Adriana Ospina and Pablo Zúñiga approached Edwards because of her work and expertise in African American and Black diaspora art.  The project received funding from U.S. Ambassador to the Organization of American States Francisco O. Mora in 2021, and Edwards curated the exhibition for an opening scheduled on March 21, 2025.
On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14151 directing the termination of federal activities relating to diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility (DEIA) and on February 6, 2025, following changes to U.S. government DEIA-related funding policy, Edwards was notified the museum removed Before the Americas from its 2025 calendar. Contemporary reporting linked the removal of the exhibition to those policy changes and to a reevaluation of federally funded programming. Donald H. Russell, curator at George Mason University (GMU) offered to host the exhibition at GMU and Edwards worked with GMU to secure additional private and institutional funding. Edwards also negotiated for the exhibition to continue at UMGC. The circumstances surrounding the exhibition were discussed in several news outlets, including Artforum, The Guardian, Le Monde, The Washington Post and The New York Times in coverage addressing arts funding, politics, censorship and minority representation.
